children: Qatar has become the latest Gulf state to tap international debt markets, launching a dual-tranche, benchmark-sized US dollar-denominated senior unsecured bond offering that is expected to be priced later today.
The five-year tranche has IPTs in the +85bp area over US Treasuries, with the 10-year at UST +95bp.

Credit Agricole CIB, Deutsche Bank, Mizuho, MUFG, Santander, SMBC are the joint lead managers, with Goldman Sachs International, HSBC, JP Morgan, QNB Capital, and Standard Chartered Bank named joint global coordinators.
HSBC is the billing and delivery bank on the five-year tranche, with Standard Chartered Bank doing the same on the 10-year issuance.
The State of Qatar, rated Aa2, Stable (Moody’s) / AA, Stable (S&P) / AA, Negative (Fitch), is acting through the Ministry of Finance, with the notes carrying an expected rated similar to the issuer.
The bonds carry a settlement date of September 28, 2026 and will be issued under Qatar’s Global Medium Term Note Programme.
A listing on the London Stock Exchange (Main Market) will follow.

Following a lull in regional debt issuance amid renewed geopolitical tensions, Saudi Arabia earlier this month raised $3.25 billion in debt through a dual-tranche US dollar-denominated sukuk offering.
(Writing by Bindu Rai, editing by Brinda Darasha)

title: Qatar mandates dual tranche sovereign USD bond, issues IPTs
